task.task_name: Review and approve a supplier invoice
task.task_description: Check a supplier invoice for authenticity, accuracy, and consistency with what the company ordered and received; resolve discrepancies with relevant parties; and approve it for payment under company policy.

operational_subtasks.description: Review the supplier details and invoice identifiers against company supplier records and available invoice evidence to assess whether the invoice appears to come from a legitimate supplier.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Per parent output of one invoice, assume this check occurs once and requires a brief review against supplier records and invoice details, with some variation in how readily records can be found. The frequency and effort are model-generated estimates; no operational time data was supplied.

operational_subtasks.description: Search invoice or accounts-payable records for a prior invoice with the same or potentially matching supplier, invoice number, amount, or other identifying details.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assume one duplicate search per invoice, usually involving a targeted lookup and comparison of identifying details. This frequency and effort are estimates; the task provides no system or workload data.

operational_subtasks.description: Confirm that a purchase order is present and compare the invoice's ordered items, prices, and applicable terms with the purchase order; identify missing or inconsistent order details.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assume this comparison occurs once per invoice and requires locating the order and checking several corresponding fields; missing or unclear order information can add review effort. These are model-generated assumptions, as no frequency or time data was supplied.

operational_subtasks.description: Compare the quantities billed with warehouse receiving records for the raw materials and identify differences between invoiced and recorded receipts.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assume one review of receiving evidence per invoice, with effort driven by finding the relevant receipt records and comparing quantities across line items. Frequency and effort are estimates; no receiving-process details were provided.

operational_subtasks.description: Recalculate or verify line extensions, subtotals, taxes, and invoice total, and assess whether taxes and any additional charges shown are consistent with the supporting order or invoice information.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assume one calculation and charge review per invoice; the number of line items and any unclear tax or additional-charge details affect effort. This is a model-generated estimate, not a measured workload.

operational_subtasks.description: For identified missing or inconsistent details, investigate the relevant order, receipt, or charge with purchasing, the warehouse, or the supplier as appropriate; obtain clarification or a correction and determine whether the discrepancy is resolved.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assume discrepancy resolution is needed for roughly 20–40% of invoices, with one or more contacts and review of the response taking more effort than a routine check. The conditional frequency and effort are estimates because the task gives no exception-rate or coordination data.

operational_subtasks.description: After checks and any necessary discrepancy resolution, determine whether the invoice satisfies company approval requirements and submit the approval for payment through the applicable process.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assume an approval decision and submission occur once per invoice that is ready for approval, requiring a brief policy and status review plus the approval action. The frequency and effort are estimates; no approval workflow details were supplied.

classified_subtasks.rationale: Supplier records and invoice evidence can be cross-checked automatically to assess whether supplier details and identifiers are legitimate.
Accounts-payable systems can search and compare invoice identifiers, suppliers, and amounts to detect duplicates.
Document extraction and workflow rules can compare invoice items, prices, and terms with purchase-order records.
Integrated invoice and receiving records can be matched to compare billed quantities with recorded receipts.
Software can recalculate invoice totals and check taxes and additional charges against available supporting information.
Automation can gather records and route inquiries, but resolving varied discrepancies with suppliers and internal parties still requires substantial recurring human follow-up.
Workflow systems can check invoice status against configured approval requirements and submit eligible invoices for payment.

activities.description: When automated checks identify a potential duplicate, supplier concern, or mismatch with order or receipt records, investigate the finding, coordinate with the relevant internal parties or supplier, obtain clarification or correction, and determine whether the discrepancy is resolved.
activities.trigger: An agentic check reports a potential duplicate, supplier concern, or inconsistency in invoice, order, receipt, calculation, tax, or charge details.
activities.expected_action: Investigate the reported exception, contact relevant parties as needed, obtain supporting information or a correction, and establish whether the invoice discrepancy is resolved.

activity_effort_estimates.rationale: Assume exceptions require human investigation and coordination on 30% of invoices. A typical occurrence is estimated to involve about 30 minutes of active review, communication, and assessment of the response; passive waiting is excluded.
assumptions: The exception frequency is modeled as 30% of parent outputs, within the supplied approximate 20–40% range.
Effort per occurrence is a planning estimate, not a measured observation.

activity_effort_estimation.baseline_rationale: Planning estimate of 45 minutes of active human work for a complete invoice review and approval before the described automation, including routine checks, expected discrepancy follow-up, and approval. This is an explicit absolute estimate and is not derived from normalized relative weights.
baseline_assumptions: The estimate represents one invoice and excludes passive waiting and machine processing.
Invoice complexity and the amount of supporting documentation vary; 45 minutes is a planning assumption rather than an observed average.
